title: Mushroom-Soy Beef Bulgogi
shortDescription: A mushroom-forward beef bulgogi with shiitake and cremini mushrooms in a savory soy, onion, garlic, and sesame marinade.
culturalContext: Mushrooms are commonly cooked alongside or in variations of bulgogi. This mushroom-heavy formulation is presented as a contemporary home-cooking adaptation, not as a separate ancient or regionally fixed dish.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

totalTime.display: 1 hour 43 minutes, including minimum marination and rest

equipment: Nonreactive mixing bowl or food-safe zip bag
Outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric tabletop grill

ingredients.preparation: sliced 3 mm / 1/8 inch thick against the grain

marinadeOrSeasoning.meatWeightCovered: 680 g / 1.5 lb thinly sliced beef plus 340 g / 12 oz mushrooms
mixOrder: Whisk soy sauce with rice syrup.
Stir in onion purée, garlic, sesame oil, ginger, and black pepper.
marinadeOrSeasoning.marinationVessel: Nonreactive bowl or food-safe zip bag set on a rimmed tray
marinadeOrSeasoning.refrigeratedMarinationTimeRange: Marinate beef 1 to 8 hours at 40°F / 4°C or below; add mushrooms only for the final 20 minutes.
marinadeOrSeasoning.maximumPracticalMarinationWarning: Do not exceed 24 hours; the salt can over-season thin beef and mushrooms absorb sauce quickly.
marinadeOrSeasoning.reserveBeforeRawContactInstruction: Reserve any serving sauce before adding the beef; the planned recipe does not require a finishing sauce.
marinadeOrSeasoning.rawContactDiscardOrReboilInstruction: Discard marinade that contacted raw beef; do not use it to dress cooked mushrooms or meat.
substitutions: Fresh oyster mushrooms may replace cremini by weight.
Certified gluten-free tamari may replace soy sauce after label review.
allergenNotes: Regular soy sauce usually contains wheat.

instructions.heading: Prepare the beef and mushrooms
instructions.action: Slice the chilled beef thinly against the grain. Brush visible soil from mushrooms with a clean towel, trim stems, and slice; do not soak the mushrooms.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Beef slices are even; mushrooms are dry and clean with broad surfaces for browning.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a separate clean board and knife for ready-to-eat garnishes after raw-beef prep, or wash and sanitize fully.

instructions.heading: Make the soy-onion marinade
instructions.action: Whisk soy sauce and rice syrup, then mix in onion purée, garlic, sesame oil, ginger, and pepper.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The marinade is uniform and lightly thickened by onion.
instructions.safetyNote: Portion any intended finishing sauce before adding raw beef.

instructions.heading: Marinate in stages
instructions.action: Coat the beef and refrigerate 1 to 8 hours. Add shiitake, cremini, and scallions for only the final 20 minutes, folding gently.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Beef is coated and mushrooms are glossy but not waterlogged.
instructions.safetyNote: Marinate only under refrigeration and discard all raw-contact liquid.

instructions.heading: Preheat the approved grill
instructions.action: Preheat to medium-high and lightly oil the clean surface. Drain excess marinade from the beef and mushrooms.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Food sizzles immediately when it touches the surface.
instructions.safetyNote: For indoor cooking, use only an electric appliance approved for indoor use and follow its ventilation and clearance directions.

instructions.heading: Cook beef and mushrooms separately
instructions.action: Cook mushrooms in a single layer until browned and tender, then move them to a clean platter. Grill beef in small batches, turning until browned and cooked through.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Mushrooms have browned edges; beef is browned and the thickest practical cluster reaches the target.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not move cooked mushrooms with raw-beef tongs unless the tongs have been washed and sanitized.

instructions.heading: Rest and combine
instructions.action: Rest the beef for at least 3 minutes, then combine it with the cooked mushrooms and scallions on the clean platter.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The mixture is glossy with distinct browned mushrooms rather than pooled liquid.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not add raw-contact marinade after cooking.

grillSetup: Preheat a clean outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric tabletop grill to medium-high, about 400–450°F / 204–232°C. Follow the appliance manual for clearance and ventilation; never use charcoal, propane, butane camping stoves, or outdoor grills indoors.
targetInternalTemperature: 145°F / 63°C in the thickest practical portion, followed by a 3-minute rest
visualDonenessCues: Mushrooms are browned and tender without pooled raw marinade.
Beef reaches 145°F / 63°C in the thickest practical cluster and rests 3 minutes.
foodSafetyNotes: Keep raw beef and its marinade separate from ready-to-eat foods; wash hands and sanitize contacted surfaces.
Use separate raw and cooked plates and utensils, or wash and sanitize them fully before reuse.
Measure the thickest practical portion with a calibrated food thermometer; grill marks and time alone do not establish doneness.
For whole-cut beef, reach 145°F / 63°C and rest for at least 3 minutes before serving.
Use only an outdoor grill or an electric tabletop appliance explicitly approved by its manufacturer for indoor use; follow ventilation and clearance instructions.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Check every packaged-ingredient label and prevent cross-contact; substitutions do not guarantee an allergen-free result.

substitutions: Use fresh oyster mushrooms for cremini by weight; texture and water release will differ.
Use certified gluten-free tamari only after checking every packaged ingredient.
ingredientSourcing: Choose dry, firm mushrooms without slimy spots or a sour odor.
Ask for thin bulgogi-cut sirloin or ribeye, or partially freeze the meat before slicing.
makeAhead: Prepare the soy-onion marinade up to 1 day ahead. Marinate the beef the same day; add mushrooms only during the final 20 minutes so they do not absorb excessive salt.
storage: Refrigerate cooked beef within 2 hours in a shallow airtight container at 40°F / 4°C or below; use within 3 days.
reheating: Reheat leftovers to 165°F / 74°C. Reheat only the portion needed and avoid prolonged cooking that toughens thin beef.
leftovers: Reheat to 165°F / 74°C and serve over rice; store fresh herbs or greens separately.
servingSuggestions: Serve with steamed rice and crisp fresh greens to balance the savory mushroom sauce.
Pair only with banchan and sauces whose allergen labels have been reviewed.

faq.question: Can I marinate the mushrooms as long as the beef?
faq.answer: No. Add them only for the final 20 minutes; their porous texture absorbs salty marinade quickly and can release water on the grill.

faq.question: Can this be cooked in a skillet?
faq.answer: Yes. Use a broad heavy skillet in batches under effective ventilation so the meat and mushrooms brown rather than steam.
